source: Cybersecurity Review Office, published on the Cyberspace Administration's site
text: The Cybersecurity Review Office, which sits in the cyberspace regulator, concludes that Micron's products did not pass its cybersecurity review, and says that operators of critical information infrastructure in China shall stop buying them. The text was published on the regulator's site. The same text welcomes companies of all countries that obey Chinese law.
words: 我国内关键信息基础设施的运营者应停止采购美光公司产品 / 网络安全审查办公室依法作出不予通过网络安全审查的结论 / 按照《网络安全法》等法律法规

text: The market regulator announces that it has opened an antitrust investigation of Nvidia. The notice is about Nvidia; it tells no buyer anything.
words: 市场监管总局依法对英伟达公司开展立案调查

text: The cyberspace regulator summons Nvidia and requires it to explain the security risks of vulnerabilities and backdoors in the H20 chips it sells to China, and to hand in supporting material. The notice is addressed to Nvidia, not to buyers.
words: 约谈了英伟达公司,要求英伟达公司就对华销售的H20算力芯片漏洞后门安全风险问题进行说明并提交相关证明材料

text: The market regulator announces a preliminary finding against Nvidia, and a further investigation, under the antitrust law and its 2020 conditions on Nvidia's purchase of Mellanox. The one-sentence notice gives no facts. By Nvidia's own account the finding concerns the "degraded products" that American export controls required it to offer the Chinese market. No page read says the case has ended: the regulator's review of its 2025 work, posted Apr 10, 2026, still lists the further investigation.
words: 市场监管总局依法决定对其实施进一步调查 / 经初步调查,英伟达公司违反《中华人民共和国反垄断法》

source: Bloomberg, Sept 27, 2024, as carried by The Business Times (Singapore)
text: Regulators discourage companies from buying Nvidia's H20, Bloomberg reports: "The policy has taken the form of guidance rather than an outright ban". It calls this "window guidance", which it explains as "instructions without the force of law". Bloomberg's report is of Sept 27; the copy used was carried on Sept 28, Singapore time.
words: The policy has taken the form of guidance rather than an outright ban / Chinese regulators have been discouraging companies from purchasing Nvidia's H20 chips / window guidance / instructions without the force of law

text: The cyberspace regulator, the state planner and the industry ministry move to dissuade companies from buying the H20, the Financial Times reports, by people it does not name. By its account the cyberspace regulator gave an informal notice, "window guidance", "instructing them to halt new orders for Nvidia's H20 chips". The same article says some firms held off H20 orders to see whether a better Nvidia chip for China would come.
words: A group of Chinese regulators have mobilised in an effort to dissuade domestic tech companies from acquiring the H20 / the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) moved in response

source: Alibaba, annual report on Form 20-F for the year to Mar 31, 2026
text: Alibaba's annual report to the US securities regulator: the cyberspace regulator "requested Chinese technology companies to halt purchases of certain chips". The sentence does not name Nvidia.
words: In September 2025, the Cyberspace Administration of China requested Chinese technology companies to halt purchases of certain chips.

text: The cyberspace regulator tells companies, ByteDance and Alibaba among them, to end their testing and orders of Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000D, the Financial Times reports, by three unnamed people. The paper calls it a ban: "The ban goes beyond earlier guidance from regulators". It reports an order told to companies, not a published rule.
words: told companies, including ByteDance and Alibaba, this week to end their testing and orders of the RTX Pro 6000D / The ban goes beyond earlier guidance from regulators

source: Reuters, Nov 5, 2025, on The Standard (Hong Kong)
text: Guidance requires new data centre projects that took state money to use only home-made AI chips, Reuters reports. It adds: "It is unclear whether the guidance applies nationwide or only to certain provinces".
words: The Chinese government has issued guidance requiring new data centre projects that have received any state funds to only use domestically-made artificial intelligence chips / It is unclear whether the guidance applies nationwide or only to certain provinces, sources said

text: At meetings on Tuesday, Jan 13, officials tell technology companies not to buy the H200 "unless necessary", Reuters reports on Jan 14, by three people; customs agents, it says, were told that week that the chips "are not permitted to enter China". Reuters wrote that it was unclear whether Beijing wanted a ban, was still weighing restrictions, or could use the measures as "a bargaining tactic in talks with Washington".
words: explicitly instructed not to purchase the chips unless necessary / Chinese customs authorities told customs agents this week that Nvidia's H200 artificial intelligence chips are not permitted to enter China

source: Nvidia, quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter to Jul 26, 2026
text: Nvidia's quarterly report to the US securities regulator: the United States granted licences for some H20 and H200 sales, "but such sales were restricted by the PRC government". It does not say by what act. The same report says Nvidia is "already effectively foreclosed from the China market by U.S. export controls".
words: but such sales were restricted by the PRC government / Beginning in February 2026, the USG granted licenses that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers
